question: Should OpenClaw adopt these four built-in deployment postures as a supported core readiness contract once the readiness prerequisites land, or keep hosting-specific conformance outside the core product for now?
rationale: This changes the supported deployment and availability contract rather than repairing an established behavior, and the protected `maintainer` label requires explicit human direction before a large core-facing surface can land.

options.title: Sponsor a bounded core profile contract
options.body: Keep the four profiles in core after the prerequisite readiness PRs land and require exact-head package-installed conformance proof before merge.

options.title: Defer the profile layer
options.body: Land only generic readiness primitives for now and revisit built-in hosting postures after maintainers define the supported deployment contract.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a bounded core profile contract
recommendation.body: Keep the four profiles in core after the prerequisite readiness PRs land and require exact-head package-installed conformance proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the only evidence-backed owner of the complete proposed readiness and hosting-profile stack, though final product acceptance remains a maintainer decision.
